title: Enforcement Decree of the Local Public Officials Education and Training Act
full_text:
Enforcement Decree of the Local Public Officials Education and Training Act

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Local Public Officials Education and Training Act and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Duties of Agencies Overseeing Education and Training)
(1) The Minister of Education and the Minister of the Interior and Safety shall perform the following duties to improve and develop education and training for local public officials: <Amended on March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014; July 26, 2017>
1. Investigations and research;
2. Guidance and support for local governments and education and training institutions (hereinafter referred to as "education and training institutions") under Article 8 of the Local Public Officials Education and Training Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") in formulating and operating education and training plans.
(2) The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall have the head of the Local Government Officials Development Institute (hereinafter referred to as the "Local Government Officials Development Institute") established pursuant to Article 4 (2) of the Public Officials Human Resources Development Act and Article 2 (1) of the Regulations on the Organization of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety and Its Affiliated Agencies perform the following duties for the effective operation, improvement, and development of education and training institutions: <Amended on March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014; February 3, 2016; July 26, 2017>
1. Research and development of education and training systems and techniques for local public officials;
2. Research and development of education and training materials and textbooks;
3. Support for education and training;
4. Promotion of cooperation among education and training institutions and collaboration with private education and training institutions;
5. Other matters concerning the improvement and development of education and training for local public officials.

Article 3 (Formulation of Education and Training Implementation Plans)
The head of a local government [including the superintendent of education of a Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Do, or Special Self-Governing Province (hereinafter referred to as a "City/Do"); hereinafter the same shall apply] and the chairperson of a local council shall formulate annual implementation plans by December 31 each year pursuant to Article 5 (3) of the Act. <Amended on November 30, 2021>

Article 4 (Classification of Education and Training)
Education and training shall be classified as follows:
1. Basic education and training: Education and training to enable candidates for new appointment, newly appointed persons, candidates for promotion, and promoted persons to develop the abilities and qualities required of public officials;
2. Specialized education and training: Education and training to enable public officials to acquire the specialized knowledge and skills necessary for the fields of duties for which they are or will be responsible;
3. Other education and training: Education and training not falling under subparagraphs 1 and 2, consisting of duty-related learning and research activities conducted by order of the head of the institution to which a public official belongs or on the public official's own initiative.

Article 5 (Methods of Education and Training)
(1) Education and training shall be conducted by methods that most efficiently achieve their purposes.
(2) Basic education and training under subparagraph 1 of Article 4 (hereinafter referred to as "basic education and training") shall be conducted at education and training institutions: Provided, That, where the Minister of Education and the Minister of the Interior and Safety recognize the appropriateness of the educational content, it may be conducted as entrusted education and training under Article 19 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "entrusted education and training") or workplace training under Article 20 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "workplace training"). <Amended on March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014; July 26, 2017>
(3) Specialized education and training under subparagraph 2 of Article 4 (hereinafter referred to as "specialized education and training") shall be conducted as workplace training: Provided, That, where it is difficult to conduct it as workplace training, it shall be conducted at an education and training institution, and where it is also difficult to conduct it at an education and training institution, it shall be conducted as entrusted education and training.
(4) Where deemed necessary, the head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council may designate education and training courses conducted by education and training institutions affiliated with central administrative agencies or other local governments, or by private education and training institutions, as specialized education and training courses for public officials under their authority. <Amended on November 30, 2021>

Article 6 (Formulation of Self-Development Plans, etc.)
(1) Local public officials shall formulate annual self-development plans in consultation with their department heads pursuant to Article 6 (1) of the Act and implement those plans.
(2) Division heads and equivalent auxiliary officials shall actively manage the implementation performance of self-development plans of public officials under their authority.
(3) The department overseeing education and training affairs shall regularly or occasionally check and inspect the implementation performance of self-development plans and endeavor to establish an educational support system.
(4) When setting work objectives for, and evaluating the achievement of objectives by, division heads and equivalent auxiliary officials, the head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council shall, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, assign responsibility for performance regarding matters such as the achievement of required education and training hours by public officials under their authority, and reflect the results of fulfilling that responsibility in the evaluations. <Amended on March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014; November 30, 2021>

Article 7 (Reflection of Completed Education and Training Hours in Promotion, etc.)
(1) For public officials in general service of Grade V or below, completed education and training hours shall be reflected in appointment by promotion in accordance with the methods and standards in Annex 1. <Amended on December 4, 2013>
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council may choose not to reflect completed education and training hours in appointment by promotion in any of the following cases: Provided, That such hours shall not be reflected in appointment by promotion in cases falling under subparagraph 1 or 2: <Amended on November 30, 2021>
1. Where a public official takes an open competitive promotion examination conducted pursuant to Article 39-2 (3) of the Local Public Officials Act;
2. Where a public official is appointed by special promotion or is given priority in taking a promotion examination pursuant to Article 39-3 of the Local Public Officials Act;
3. Where a public official fails to complete the education and training hours required for appointment by promotion due to special reasons related to the performance of duties, and the head of the local government or the chairperson of the local council deems it necessary.
(3) The annual completed education and training hours to be applied to appointment by promotion under paragraph (1), the content of education and training, and other matters necessary for operating education and training shall be determined by the head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council within the scope prescribed in this Decree and separately determined by the Minister of Education and the Minister of the Interior and Safety. In such cases, the head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council may determine different requirements for units classified according to appropriate criteria, such as occupational series or grade. <Amended on March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014; July 26, 2017; November 30, 2021>

Article 8 (Duties of Education and Training Officers)
An education and training officer appointed under Article 7 of the Act shall oversee the following duties:
1. Formulation of education and training plans for the relevant local government and its affiliated institutions;
2. Securing education and training expenses necessary for the education and training of public officials under their authority;
3. Consultation and coordination on other policies to promote education and training.

Article 9 (Conduct of Integrated Education and Training)
(1) Integrated education and training under Article 8 (2) and (4) of the Act shall be conducted by entrusting it to the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayor, Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Do Governor, or Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter referred to as a "Mayor/Do Governor") of a jurisdiction in which a local public officials training institute under paragraph (1) of that Article (hereinafter referred to as a "local public officials training institute") is established. <Amended on March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014; July 26, 2017; May 21, 2019; November 30, 2021>
(2) The head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council who intend to entrust education and training under paragraph (1) shall, following consultation with the Mayor/Do Governor receiving the entrustment, establish and publicly notify an agreement that includes the following matters: <Amended on November 30, 2021>
1. The entrusting local government and the City/Do receiving the entrustment;
2. The content and scope of the education and training being entrusted;
3. Methods of managing and conducting the education and training being entrusted;
4. Allocation and disbursement methods for expenses incurred in managing and conducting the education and training being entrusted;
5. Other matters necessary for entrusting education and training.
(3) The head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council who have entrusted education and training under paragraph (1) shall not alter or terminate the entrustment while an education and training course is in progress unless there are special circumstances. To alter or terminate the entrustment, they shall consult with the Mayor/Do Governor receiving the entrustment and publicly notify the details. <Amended on November 30, 2021>
(4) Deleted. <May 21, 2019>
(5) Ordinances or rules on the management and conduct of entrusted education and training shall also apply to the City/Do receiving the entrustment, except as otherwise provided in the agreement under paragraph (2).

Article 10 (Education and Training Institutions)
(1) Matters concerning the organization of local public officials training institutes shall be prescribed separately by Presidential Decree.
(2) "Education and training prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 8 (3) of the Act means the following education and training: <Amended on March 23, 2013; November 19, 2014; July 26, 2017>
1. Basic education and training for candidates for promotion to Grade V (excluding cases in which the Minister of the Interior and Safety deems it necessary at the request of a Mayor/Do Governor);
2. Long-term education and training conducted under a domestic entrusted education and training plan formulated by the Minister of the Interior and Safety pursuant to Article 19 (2) of the Act;
3. Other education and training that the Minister of the Interior and Safety deems to require nationwide integrated operation.
(3) "Education and training institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 8 (5) of the Act means education training institutes affiliated with superintendents of education: Provided, That, in the case of education and training falling under any of the following subparagraphs, the term means the National Education Training Institute under Article 2 (1) of the Regulations on the Organization of the Ministry of Education and Its Affiliated Agencies: <Amended on March 23, 2013>
1. Basic education and training for candidates for promotion to Grade V;
2. Long-term education and training for local public officials of Grade V or above conducted under a domestic entrusted education and training plan formulated by the Minister of Education pursuant to Article 19 (2) of the Act;
3. Other education and training for local public officials of Grade V or above that the Minister of Education deems to require nationwide integrated operation.

Article 11 (Selection of Persons to Receive Education and Training)
(1) The head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council shall select public officials under their jurisdiction who meet the selection criteria for each education and training course as persons to receive education and training, taking into account their grades, occupational series, assigned duties, career histories, health conditions, and other relevant matters. <Amended on 2021.11.30>
(2) The head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council shall notify the head of the education and training institution of the list of persons selected to receive education and training no later than 10 days before the education and training begins. <Amended on 2021.11.30>
(3) If the head of an education and training institution who receives notification under paragraph (2) considers that a person selected to receive education and training falls substantially outside the selection criteria for the relevant education and training course, the head may request that the person be replaced. In such cases, the head of the local government and the chairperson of the local council shall select a replacement and provide notification thereof without delay. <Amended on 2021.11.30>
(4) A public official selected to receive education and training shall register with the education and training institution before the education and training begins and shall comply with the instructions of the head of that institution during the education and training period.
(5) The head of an education and training institution may collect and use the following personal information concerning persons selected to receive education and training to improve educational outcomes and efficiently manage such persons:
1. Affiliation, name, position, and grade;
2. Date of birth, date of appointment, and years of service;
3. Assigned duties and contact information.

Article 12 (Education and Training and Personnel Management)
(1) The head of a local government (including the heads of its subordinate institutions) and the chairperson of a local council shall, when assigning candidates for new appointment and newly appointed public officials to positions in their assigned grades and fields of duties, assign them only after they have completed basic education and training courses corresponding to those grades and fields of duties. <Amended on 2021.11.30>
(2) When making appointments by promotion to Grade V, the head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council shall, unless there is a special reason to the contrary, make such appointments from among persons who have completed the basic education and training course for candidates for promotion to Grade V. <Amended on 2021.11.30>
(3) The head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council shall, unless there is a special reason to the contrary, assign local public officials who have received education and training to positions in fields related to the education and training they have completed. <Amended on 2021.11.30>
(4) When providing entrusted education and training, the head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council shall designate in advance the fields of assignment following completion of the education and training and provide the education and training accordingly, and shall, unless there is a special reason to the contrary, assign the officials to positions in those fields after they have completed the education and training. <Amended on 2021.11.30>

Article 13 (Scope of Education and Training Expenses to Be Borne)
(1) The scope of education and training expenses to be borne by the head of the institution to which a public official belongs pursuant to Article 17 of the Act shall be as follows:
1. Expenses necessary for engaging lecturers, such as lecturers' allowances;
2. Expenses for teaching materials, experiments, and practical training;
3. Expenses for field visits and overseas training;
4. Other education expenses incurred in providing education and training, such as public utility charges.
(2) The head of the institution to which a public official belongs shall bear the education and training expenses under paragraph (1) only when requested by the head of the education and training institution.
(3) Notwithstanding paragraphs (1) and (2), where education and training is entrusted to a university, a private education and training institution, or a similar institution, the head of the institution to which the public official receiving the education and training belongs may bear the education and training expenses in full.

Article 14 (Payment of Travel Expenses for Education and Training) The head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council shall pay travel expenses for education and training, within budgetary limits, to public officials under their jurisdiction who have been selected to receive education and training. <Amended on 2021.11.30>

Article 15 (Criteria for Securing Education and Training Expenses) The Minister of Education and the Minister of the Interior and Safety may establish criteria for securing education and training expenses pursuant to Article 18 (1) of the Act by analyzing the ratio of education and training expenses to personnel expenses of local governments, education and training expenses per public official, demand for education and training, and other relevant matters. <Amended on 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>

Article 16 (Evaluation of Education and Training)
(1) The head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council shall evaluate the content, methods, outcomes, and other aspects of education and training for local public officials periodically or as necessary to improve and develop such education and training. <Amended on 2021.11.30>
(2) The Minister of Education and the Minister of the Interior and Safety shall check and evaluate the results of education and training provided by their subordinate education and training institutions or by local governments periodically or as necessary. <Amended on 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>

Article 17 (Requests for Education and Training Materials, etc.) The Minister of Education, the Minister of the Interior and Safety, the head of a local government, the chairperson of a local council, and the head of an education and training institution may, if deemed necessary for education and training, request the heads of relevant institutions to provide necessary cooperation, such as producing teaching materials and audiovisual materials or providing lecturers. <Amended on 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26, 2021.11.30>

CHAPTER II EDUCATION AND TRAINING AT EDUCATION AND TRAINING INSTITUTIONS

Article 18 (Education and Training Plans of Education and Training Institutions)
(1) The head of an education and training institution shall prepare an education and training plan containing the following matters in accordance with the master plan for education and training and annual implementation plans established by the head of the local government and the chairperson of the local council pursuant to Article 5 of the Act, and shall report it to the head of the local government to which the institution belongs by December 31 each year: <Amended on 2021.11.30>
1. Basic direction of education and training;
2. Plans for establishing education and training courses;
3. Objectives, content, duration, target participants, and number of participants for each education and training course;
4. Results of surveys of demand for education and training and plans for selecting persons to receive education and training;
5. Plans for compiling teaching materials and methods for assessing education and training performance;
6. Other matters necessary for education and training.
(2) The head of an education and training institution shall, without delay, notify the heads of relevant local governments, the chairpersons of relevant local councils, and the heads of relevant institutions of the education and training plan reported under paragraph (1), so that preparations for education and training, such as the selection of persons to receive education and training, can proceed smoothly. <Amended on 2021.11.30>
(3) The head of an education and training institution shall evaluate the outcomes of education and training each year and reflect the results in the education and training plan for the following year.

Article 19 (Education and Training Deliberation Committee)
(1) The head of an education and training institution shall establish an education and training deliberation committee composed of outside experts, recipients of education and training, relevant public officials, and other relevant persons to deliberate on important matters concerning the operation of education and training, such as the formulation of education and training plans, evaluation of outcomes, and establishment and abolition of education and training courses.
(2) Detailed matters concerning the composition and operation of the education and training deliberation committee under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by the head of the education and training institution.

Article 20 (Assessment of Education and Training Performance and Completion)
(1) The head of an education and training institution shall assess trainees' education and training performance in accordance with objective and fair assessment criteria and methods.
(2) Education and training shall be deemed completed if the trainee receives a score of at least 60 points out of 100.
(3) The head of an education and training institution may commend trainees whose education and training performance is outstanding.
(4) Within 10 days after the education and training course ends, the head of the education and training institution shall notify the heads of the institutions to which persons who have completed the education and training belong of those persons' education and training scores.

Article 21 (Measures against Persons Who Fail to Attain the Completion Score)
(1) The head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council shall require public officials under their jurisdiction and candidates for new appointment whose education and training scores fall below the completion score under Article 20 (2) to receive education and training again. <Amended on 2013.12.4, 2021.11.30>
(2) Where the head of the institution to which a person belongs considers that the person, after receiving education and training again under paragraph (1), has again failed to attain the completion score and has an extremely poor work performance such that grounds exist for dismissal ex officio or disciplinary action under Article 62 or 69 of the Local Public Officials Act, the head may take measures such as requesting a resolution on disciplinary action from the competent personnel committee.
(3) The head of an institution who has taken measures under paragraph (2) shall notify the head of the relevant education and training institution of that fact.

Article 22 (Expulsion)
(1) The head of an education and training institution shall expel a trainee and notify the head of the institution to which the trainee belongs if the trainee falls under any of the following:
1. Where a person selected to receive education and training has another person receive the education and training on their behalf;
2. Where the trainee is absent without a justifiable reason;
3. Where the trainee seriously neglects classes or cheats during an examination;
4. Where the trainee fails to comply with the instructions of the head of the education and training institution concerning education and training;
5. Where the trainee is unable to continue receiving education and training due to illness or other personal circumstances.
(2) Where the head of an institution considers that a public official belonging to the institution who has been expelled on any of the grounds specified in paragraph (1) 1 through 4 or has avoided registration under Article 11 (4) without a justifiable reason falls under any of the subparagraphs of Article 69 (1) of the Local Public Officials Act, the head may request a resolution on disciplinary action from the competent personnel committee.
(3) The head of an institution who has requested a resolution on disciplinary action under paragraph (2) shall notify the head of the relevant education and training institution of that fact.

Article 23 (Qualification Standards for Teaching Personnel) Teaching personnel of an education and training institution shall be persons who fall under any of the following: <Amended on 2012.2.29>
1. A person with at least three years of practical work, research, or teaching experience related to the field they will be responsible for;
2. A person who holds a certificate of qualification related to the field they will be responsible for;
3. A person who holds a master's degree or higher degree in the field they will be responsible for;
4. A person who has completed at least six months of education and training in the field they will be responsible for;
5. A person who is qualified as a professor, associate professor, or assistant professor under Article 16 of the Higher Education Act and Article 2 of the Regulations on Qualification Standards, etc. for University Faculty Members;
6. Any other person who has qualifications or abilities equivalent to those specified in subparagraphs 1 through 5 and meets the qualification or ability requirements prescribed by the Mayor/Do Governor or superintendent of education who established the education and training institution.

Article 24 (Grounds for Disqualification of Teaching Personnel) A person who has been subject to disciplinary action and for whom two years have not elapsed since the expiration of the period of that action, or a person for whom one year has not elapsed since the end of a measure removing the person from their position, may not be appointed as teaching personnel of an education and training institution.

Article 25 (Service Period, etc. of Teaching Personnel)
(1) The service period of teaching personnel at an education and training institution shall be two years: Provided, That the head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council may shorten or extend that period where special grounds exist. <Amended on 2021.11.30>
(2) The head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council shall give preferential treatment in promotion or transfer to public officials who have faithfully completed their service as teaching personnel, unless special grounds exist. <Amended on 2021.11.30>

Article 26 (Education of Teaching Personnel)
The head of the Local Government Officials Development Institute shall establish an education course for teaching personnel at the beginning of each year and conduct education and training to enable newly appointed teaching personnel to acquire the necessary knowledge, skills, and general competencies. <Amended on 2017.7.26>

Article 27 (Institutional Regulations, etc.)
The head of an education and training institution may prescribe and implement, through institutional regulations or the like, the content and methods of education and training to be conducted at the institution, the guidance of trainees, and other matters concerning education and training.

CHAPTER III WORKPLACE TRAINING

Article 28 (Content of Workplace Training)
The content of workplace training shall be as follows:
1. Education on topical policies of the Government or the relevant local government and mental training;
2. Education and training necessary for newly appointed public officials to adapt to the workplace and practical duties;
3. Education and training necessary for the performance of duties by public officials whose assigned positions have changed;
4. Education and training for acquiring specialized knowledge and skills by department or field of duties.

Article 29 (Conduct of Workplace Training)
(1) The head of a local government (including the heads of its subordinate institutions; hereafter in this Article the same shall apply) and the chairperson of a local council shall conduct systematic workplace training for public officials under their authority by department or field of duties, regularly or as needed. <Amended on 2021.11.30>
(2) The head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council shall designate an education and training guidance officer for each local public official serving a probationary period and conduct systematic workplace training to enable the official to acquire an understanding of the organization and functions of the relevant institution and the knowledge, skills, general competencies, etc. necessary for the performance of duties. <Amended on 2021.11.30>
(3) Where the head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council operate specialized education and training courses as workplace training, they shall prescribe and implement specific standards for the evaluation and completion of education and training, measures for persons whose scores fall below the score required for completion, and other matters concerning the conduct of education and training. <Amended on 2021.11.30>

CHAPTER IV ENTRUSTED EDUCATION AND TRAINING

Article 30 (Plans for Entrusted Education and Training)
(1) A plan for entrusted education and training under Article 19 (1) and (2) of the Act shall include the following matters: Provided, That subparagraphs 5 and 7 shall apply only to education and training lasting at least six months:
1. The purpose and content of education and training;
2. The education and training institution and the duration of education and training;
3. The number of persons by type and field of education and training;
4. Eligibility requirements for persons to receive education and training and the methods and procedures for their selection;
5. Plans for assignment to positions after completion of education and training;
6. An itemized statement of education and training expenses and matters concerning responsibility for those expenses;
7. Matters concerning service obligations;
8. Other matters necessary for education and training.
(2) The head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council shall take necessary measures, such as selecting persons to receive education and training and bearing education and training expenses, in accordance with a domestic entrusted education and training plan established by the Minister of Education or the Minister of the Interior and Safety under Article 19 (2) of the Act. <Amended on 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26, 2021.11.30>

Article 31 (Selection of Persons to Receive Entrusted Education and Training)
(1) The head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council shall select persons to receive entrusted education and training from among public officials who meet all of the following requirements: <Amended on 2021.11.30>
1. A person with a firm sense of national identity and unwavering loyalty to the State;
2. A person with excellent work performance;
3. A person with the necessary educational background, career experience, etc.;
4. A person able to remain in service for a substantial period after completing education and training;
5. In the case of overseas entrusted education and training, a person with the necessary foreign language proficiency.
(2) A person who has received a disciplinary disposition may not be selected to receive entrusted education and training lasting at least six months until one year has elapsed from the date on which the period of that disposition expired: Provided, That this shall not apply to a person who received a disciplinary disposition mitigated in accordance with the standards for determining disciplinary penalties under Article 8 of the Regulations on Disciplinary Action and Appeals for Local Public Officials, on the grounds that the misconduct was recognized as having arisen from negligence in the course of diligently and actively carrying out duties.

Article 32 (Guidance and Supervision of Public Officials Receiving Entrusted Education and Training)
(1) To achieve the objectives of entrusted education and training, the head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council shall regularly or as needed ascertain the status of the education and training of public officials receiving entrusted education and training and provide the guidance and supervision necessary for their education and training and service. <Amended on 2021.11.30>
(2) Public officials receiving entrusted education and training shall endeavor to achieve the objectives of the education and training, fulfill their obligations as public officials receiving education and training, including maintaining their dignity as public officials and complying with the institutional regulations of the education and training institution during the education and training period, and comply with instructions given by the head of the local government or the chairperson of the local council to which they belong. They shall return to their duties without delay after completing the education and training. <Amended on 2021.11.30>
(3) Public officials receiving entrusted education and training shall report to the head of the local government or the chairperson of the local council to which they belong their whereabouts and personal circumstances, their education and training grades or progress and the results of their education and training, and other matters requested by the head of the local government or the chairperson of the local council. <Amended on 2021.11.30>
(4) Where a public official receiving entrusted education and training falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the official shall immediately report to the head of the local government or the chairperson of the local council to which the official belongs and follow their instructions: <Amended on 2021.11.30>
1. Where the official intends to change the education and training institution, the education and training period, or the like;
2. Where a change in the official's personal circumstances, such as illness or an accident, occurs to an extent that interferes with education and training;
3. Where the official intends to receive scholarships, donations, contributions, or the like other than education and training expenses paid by the State or a local government.
(5) A public official who intends to resign while receiving entrusted education and training overseas shall submit a letter of resignation to the head of the local government or the chairperson of the local council to which the official belongs after returning to the country. <Amended on 2021.11.30>

Article 33 (Orders to Return)
Where a public official receiving entrusted education and training seriously departs from the objectives of the education and training by violating the obligations or instructions under Article 32, or becomes unable to continue the training due to illness, accidents, or other unavoidable grounds, the head of the local government and the chairperson of the local council to which the official belongs shall order the official to return without delay. <Amended on 2021.11.30>

Article 34 (Service Obligations)
(1) The head of a local government or the chairperson of a local council shall require a public official who has received entrusted education and training for at least six months (including a person who returned during entrusted education and training after receiving education and training for at least six months) to serve in a field of duties related to the field of education and training for the period specified in the following subparagraphs, subject to a maximum of six years: Provided, That the service obligation may be waived where it is difficult to impose the obligation or where special circumstances arise after its imposition that make it impossible to fulfill the obligation. <Amended on 2021.11.30>
1. Domestic entrusted education and training: A period equal to the education and training period (in the case of entrusted education and training conducted only after working hours, a period equivalent to 50 percent of the education and training period);
2. Overseas entrusted education and training: A period equal to twice the education and training period.
(2) The head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council shall immediately report to the Minister of Education or the Minister of the Interior and Safety any public official who is separated from service, placed on a leave of absence, or transferred to a State agency or an institution of another local government during the mandatory service period under paragraph (1). <Amended on 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26, 2021.11.30>
(3) Where a public official who has received entrusted education and training is not serving in a field of duties related to the field of education and training as required under paragraph (1), the Minister of Education and the Minister of the Interior and Safety may request rectification from the head of the relevant local government or the chairperson of the relevant local council. <Amended on 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26, 2021.11.30>
(4) Periods of leave of absence under Article 63 (1) 1, 2, and 4 and (2) 2, 4, 5, and 6 of the Local Public Officials Act and periods of release from position under Article 65-3 of the Local Public Officials Act shall not count toward the mandatory service period under paragraph (1): Provided, That periods of leave of absence due to illness arising from official duties shall be counted.

Article 35 (Measures for Repayment of Expenses due to Violations of Obligations, etc.)
(1) Where a public official undergoing or having completed entrusted education and training falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council shall require the official to repay all or part of the expenses incurred for the official's entrusted education and training, as prescribed by ordinance within the scope of the standards for calculating repayment amounts specified in Annex 2: <Amended on 2021.11.30>
1. Where the official is separated from service during training (excluding separation from service due to illness, accidents, or other unavoidable grounds);
2. Where the official is returned before completing the education and training for violating the obligations or instructions under Article 32, or, without special grounds, abandons education and training midway or is dismissed from the education and training;
3. Where, despite having received an order to return under Article 33, the official fails to return by the designated date without justifiable grounds, or is separated from service after returning due to grounds that arose during the education and training;
4. Where the official fails to fulfill the service obligation under Article 34 (1).
(2) Where a public official undergoing or having completed entrusted education and training does not repay all or part of the expenses, the head of a local government and the chairperson of a local council may demand performance of the guarantee obligation from the official's guarantor (including an insurance company that has issued a guarantee insurance policy under the Insurance Business Act). <Newly inserted on 2021.11.30>

Article 36 (Calculation of Expenses)
(1) Expenses incurred for entrusted education and training as referred to in the part of Article 35 (1) other than its subparagraphs shall be all expenses paid by the local government during the entrusted education and training period (including travel expenses but excluding remuneration; hereinafter the same shall apply). <Amended on 2021.11.30>
(2) In the case of entrusted education and training provided on condition that a foreign government agency, school, or the like pays all or part of the expenses of the entrusted education and training, notwithstanding paragraph (1), all expenses paid by the foreign government agency, school, or the like during the entrusted education and training period shall be deemed expenses incurred for entrusted education and training, up to an amount equivalent to the remuneration paid during that period: Provided, That subsidies received as compensation for lectures or assistance with research shall not be included.

Article 37 (Detailed Implementation Guidelines for Entrusted Education and Training)
Except as provided in this Decree, matters necessary for the implementation of entrusted education and training, such as procedures for selecting persons to receive entrusted education and training, guidance and supervision of persons receiving entrusted education and training, and payment of education and training expenses, shall be governed by the provisions applicable to entrusted education and training for State public officials.

Article 38 (Processing of Unique Identification Information)
The Minister of Education, the Minister of the Interior and Safety, the head of a local government, the chairperson of a local council, and the head of an education and training institution may process data containing resident registration numbers, passport numbers, or alien registration numbers under subparagraph 1, 2, or 4 of Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act where this is unavoidable for the performance of education and training affairs under Article 4. <Amended on 2021.11.30>
